question: How do I sort an MS Access query so rows matching the most of three OR'd conditions come first, with ties broken by three other columns?
answer: ORDER BY IIF(col1 = 1,1,0) + IIF(col2 = 2,1,0) + IIF(col3 = 3,1,0) DESC, col4, col5, col6
support: ORDER BY IIF(col1 = 1,1,0) + IIF(col2 = 2,1,0) + IIF(col3 = 3,1,0) DESC

question: Why doesn't granting all permissions on a subnet ARN let IAM users fully manage instances in that subnet, and which EC2 action is the example of this limitation?
answer: AttachVolume only supports restricting by volume id, so subnet-level permissions don't cover it.
support: AttachVolume only supports restricting by volume id

question: Can I get hosts in one subnet to reach another subnet by poisoning their ARP tables with the other network's addresses?
answer: No. ARP isn't consulted for off-link networks; traffic follows the route table (default route), and sane hosts ignore such martian entries.
support: any sane host will ignore such martians

question: What attack becomes possible against a company that adds addresses to its newsletter list without any confirmation step?
answer: An attacker programmatically subscribes many real users and keeps re-subscribing them after they unsubscribe, so the company ends up sending lots of spam.
support: An attacker programmatically subscribes many real users.

question: In TCP as defined in RFC 793, what inequality must hold for an incoming ACK to count as an acceptable acknowledgment?
answer: SND.UNA < SEG.ACK =< SND.NXT (oldest unacknowledged sequence number below the ACK, ACK at most the next sequence number to send).

question: In a single-page AJAX app, how can one endpoint decide whether to serve the login page or the main application page without trusting client-side JavaScript?
answer: It returns the login page or the application page depending on whether a valid 'login' is set in the server-side session; later AJAX calls send the session cookie.
support: it just returned either a login page or the main application page depending on whether a valid 'login' was set in the server-side session

question: In Linux, does every process get its own page table structure, and which part of the address space do those tables share between processes?
answer: Each process has its own page table structure, and the kernel portion of the address space is shared between processes.
support: Each process has its own page table structure, which is set up so that the kernel portion of the address space is shared between processes.

question: In SQL Server, how can a view compute a cumulative total of each person's plan deductions ordered by plan code and report only the amount over a 400 limit as out-of-pocket?
answer: Self-join payroll on PersonID with p2.PlanCode <= p1.PlanCode, group by, and use case when sum(p2.Deduction) < 400 then 0 else sum(p2.Deduction) - 400 end.
support: case when sum(p2.Deduction) < 400 then 0 else sum(p2.Deduction) - 400 end as OOP

question: In a Jenkins scripted pipeline, how do I list the commit messages and authors of every build since the last successful one?
answer: Recursively walk getPreviousBuild() collecting builds whose result isn't SUCCESS, then loop rawBuild.changeSets entries (entry.msg, entry.author) in an @NonCPS method.

question: Is there a recommended write-up, by the author of the book Cisco Firewalls, on where to place an IPS or IDS relative to the firewall?
How can the flood of EU cookie consent banners make users less safe when a genuinely important security prompt appears?
answer: Dialog box fatigue: users get in the habit of clicking OK to dismiss dialogs, so they may click OK on an important security decision.

question: What ownership and permissions must the directories above chrooted internal-sftp users' home directories have, and what can't the users do to their top-level directory?
answer: Root-owned parent dir with 555 permissions; user dirs created by root, owned by each user. Users can't delete or rename those user dirs.
support: Root-owned dir should have 555 permissions and user-dirs should be created by root and owned by specific user.

question: How often should a team lead give performance feedback and set expectations to head off conflicts between developers, according to one manager who ran a team of 10 for two years without conflict?
support: Give regular feedback on performance and set expectations preferrably monthly.

question: mq-deadline is built into my kernel but /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler doesn't offer it for my SCSI disk. Which kernel config option do I also need to enable?
answer: CONFIG_SCSI_MQ_DEFAULT (SCSI: use blk-mq I/O path by default), under Device Drivers -> SCSI device support.
support: You also need to enable CONFIG_SCSI_MQ_DEFAULT

question: In SSRS, the page setup print options don't change my report's orientation. What do I set in BIDS instead?
answer: The report's Height and Width properties inside BIDS; orientation in SSRS is controlled by these values.
support: You will need to use the Height/Width property of the report inside BIDS. Orientation in SSRS is controlled by setting these values.

question: How can one Docker image holding many Python scripts launch a different script in each container by changing only an environment variable?
answer: Define CMD as cd /usr/src/app && python -u $RUN_SCRIPT and set RUN_SCRIPT in each container's environment.

question: If a switch already forwards frames by MAC address instead of broadcasting them, what is the major underlying goal of using VLANs?
answer: To partition one physical switch into multiple logical LANs, e.g. ports per department, so no dedicated LAN hardware is needed for each.
support: its major underlying goal was to partition a physical LAN device (switch, bridge) into multiple logical portions (VLANs)

question: Why does Yubico not let users supply their own key material to an authenticator, in terms of what its attestation can promise?
answer: Yubico couldn't guarantee, via attestation to their root cert, that the key material was securely generated by them and stored only on the authenticator.
support: if an attestation is verified up to our root cert, we guarantee that the associated keypair comes from a Yubikey

question: Our S3 bucket size has ballooned but listing the objects doesn't account for it. What is silently consuming the space, and how was it cleaned up?
answer: Parts of failed/aborted multipart uploads, kept indefinitely; fixed with a lifecycle rule removing aborted multipart upload chunks after 1 day (versioning enabled temporarily).
support: S3 keeps every uploaded part of every failed multipart upload indefinitely by default!
